long_biography.plain_text:
Growing up in Chicago public housing, Richard Portillo left school for the Marine Corps and returned to a succession of manual jobs. Seeking independence, he and his wife Sharon committed their savings to a tiny trailer in Villa Park. Portillo learned restaurant operations by studying competitors, then expanded the Dog House into a multistate chain distinguished by drive-through service, broad menus and heavily themed interiors.

Portillo sold the debt-free business after five decades and shifted from restaurant operator to landlord and investor. He repurchased many restaurant properties on long leases, assembled industrial and retail holdings, and developed or acquired housing across several states. He also remains a restaurant principal through a major Disney Springs venue and selected Portillo’s locations. The original chain created his fortune; the post-sale portfolio now makes real estate his principal current business.
